verdict.rationale: The evidence pack never documents an in-process local-evaluation mode in which server SDKs evaluate flags from a cached environment ruleset without a network call per check. The closest item is the self-hosted Edge Proxy, a separate service that acts as a local cache near your servers; SDKs still make requests to it, so it is an adjacent architecture rather than SDK local evaluation. Community discussion also describes Flagsmith as doing 'primarily server-side eval.'

support.subject: As a platform engineer, my server SDKs evaluate flags locally from a cached ruleset — microsecond decisions with no network call per flag check

citations.quote: The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
The proxy also acts as a local cache, allowing you to make requests to the proxy without hitting the Core API.
